rounds.note: A four-join group-by in SQL; one pattern and implicit grouping in Cypher.
rounds.question: Open issues by business unit and rating
rounds.sql:
-- Round 1: open issues by business unit and rating
SELECT b.business_unit_id, b.name AS business_unit_name, i.rating,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.issue_id) AS open_issues
FROM issue AS i
JOIN against_risk AS ar ON ar.issue_id = i.issue_id
JOIN exposed_to AS ex ON ex.risk_id = ar.risk_id
JOIN business_unit_owns_auditable_entity AS o ON o.auditable_entity_id = ex.auditable_entity_id
JOIN business_unit AS b ON b.business_unit_id = o.business_unit_id
WHERE i.closed_date IS NULL
GROUP BY b.business_unit_id, b.name, i.rating
ORDER BY b.business_unit_id, i.rating;

rounds.note: A CTE and an anti-join in SQL; a WITH stage and an EXISTS subquery in Cypher.
rounds.question: High risks with stale coverage, on canonical items
rounds.sql:
-- Round 2: High canonical risks with stale coverage
WITH fresh AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.canonical_risk_id
  FROM risk_maps_to_canonical AS m
  JOIN mitigates AS mi ON mi.risk_id = m.risk_id
  JOIN audit_tested_control_ia AS t ON t.control_id = mi.control_id
  JOIN audit AS a ON a.audit_id = t.audit_id
  WHERE a.end_date >= :cutoff)
SELECT m.canonical_risk_id, MAX(CASE WHEN m.source = 'IA' THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END) AS has_ia_member
FROM risk_maps_to_canonical AS m
JOIN risk AS r ON r.risk_id = m.risk_id
LEFT JOIN fresh AS f ON f.canonical_risk_id = m.canonical_risk_id
WHERE f.canonical_risk_id IS NULL
GROUP BY m.canonical_risk_id
HAVING MAX(r.inherent_rating = 'High') = 1
ORDER BY m.canonical_risk_id;

rounds.note: Three joins and a top-3 in SQL; one four-node pattern in Cypher.
rounds.question: Shared-system blast radius: the 3 systems reaching the most auditable entities
rounds.sql:
-- Round 3: shared-system blast radius
SELECT s.system_id, s.name AS system_name, COUNT(DISTINCT ex.auditable_entity_id) AS entities
FROM system AS s
JOIN depends_on AS d ON d.system_id = s.system_id
JOIN mitigates AS mi ON mi.control_id = d.control_id
JOIN exposed_to AS ex ON ex.risk_id = mi.risk_id
GROUP BY s.system_id, s.name
ORDER BY entities DESC, system_name
LIMIT 3;

rounds.note: Three joins counting rows in SQL; one five-node path counted in Cypher.
rounds.question: Every path from a regulation to a business unit
rounds.sql:
-- Round 4: every path from a regulation to a business unit
SELECT rq.regulation_id, o.business_unit_id, COUNT(*) AS paths
FROM requires AS rq
JOIN mitigates AS mi ON mi.control_id = rq.control_id
JOIN exposed_to AS ex ON ex.risk_id = mi.risk_id
JOIN business_unit_owns_auditable_entity AS o ON o.auditable_entity_id = ex.auditable_entity_id
GROUP BY rq.regulation_id, o.business_unit_id
ORDER BY rq.regulation_id, o.business_unit_id;

rounds.note: SQL adds one table and a recursive CTE; the graph must first turn vendors into nodes and edges.
rounds.question: A third-party register arrives: which auditable entities are exposed to the vendor most others rely on, directly or only through fourth parties?
rounds.sql:
-- Round 5 setup: the fourth-party register arrives as a new table
CREATE TEMP TABLE vendor_relies_on (vendor TEXT NOT NULL, relies_on TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO vendor_relies_on (vendor, relies_on)
VALUES (:vendor, :relies_on);

-- Round 5: entities exposed to a vendor, directly or through fourth parties
WITH RECURSIVE upstream(vendor) AS (
  SELECT :vendor
  UNION
  SELECT r.vendor
  FROM vendor_relies_on AS r
  JOIN upstream AS u ON r.relies_on = u.vendor)
SELECT p.auditable_entity_id,
  CASE WHEN MAX(s.vendor = :vendor) = 1 THEN 'direct' ELSE 'fourth_party_only' END AS exposure
FROM auditable_entity_performs_process AS p
JOIN process_runs_on_system AS ro ON ro.process_id = p.process_id
JOIN system AS s ON s.system_id = ro.system_id
JOIN upstream AS u ON u.vendor = s.vendor
GROUP BY p.auditable_entity_id
ORDER BY p.auditable_entity_id;

rounds.cypher:
// Round 6: repeat findings in disguise
MATCH (c:Control {source: 'IA'})<-[:AGAINST]-(i:Issue)
WITH c, collect(i) AS issues, count(DISTINCT substring(i.opened_date, 0, 4)) AS years
WHERE years >= 2
UNWIND issues AS i
RETURN c.id AS control_id, i.issue_id AS issue_id, i.opened_date AS opened_date, i.title AS title
ORDER BY control_id, issue_id;
rounds.note: A grouped CTE joined back in SQL; collect and unwind in Cypher. Links and dates, never titles.
rounds.question: Repeat findings in disguise: IA controls with issues in two or more years, and their issues
rows: Weaknesses noted in data quality rules
Weaknesses noted in reconciling item aging
Gaps in reconciling item aging evidence
Reconciling item aging not performed as designed
Weaknesses noted in security alert triage
Weaknesses noted in capital stress tests
Capital stress tests not performed as designed
rounds.sql:
-- Round 6: repeat findings in disguise
WITH repeat AS (
  SELECT ac.control_id
  FROM issue_against_control_ia AS ac
  JOIN issue AS i ON i.issue_id = ac.issue_id
  GROUP BY ac.control_id
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT substr(i.opened_date, 1, 4)) >= 2)
SELECT ac.control_id, i.issue_id, i.opened_date, i.title
FROM repeat AS r
JOIN issue_against_control_ia AS ac ON ac.control_id = r.control_id
JOIN issue AS i ON i.issue_id = ac.issue_id
ORDER BY ac.control_id, i.issue_id;

rounds.cypher:
// Round 7: year-over-year findings by ERM L1 (regulator, self-identified and 2nd-line issues)
MATCH (l1:TaxonomyNode {source: 'ERM', level: 1})-[:PARENT_OF*2]->(:TaxonomyNode)
  -[:CLASSIFIES]->(:Risk)<-[:AGAINST]-(i:Issue)
WHERE i.source <> 'IA'
RETURN l1.id AS l1_node_id, l1.name AS l1_name, substring(i.opened_date, 0, 4) AS year,
  count(DISTINCT i) AS issues
ORDER BY l1_node_id, year;
rounds.note: Two parent joins up the taxonomy in SQL; a fixed two-hop path in Cypher.
rounds.question: Year-over-year findings by ERM L1 (regulator, self-identified and 2nd-line issues)
rounds.sql:
-- Round 7: year-over-year findings by ERM L1 (regulator, self-identified and 2nd-line issues)
SELECT l1.taxonomy_node_id AS l1_node_id, l1.name AS l1_name, substr(i.opened_date, 1, 4) AS year,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.issue_id) AS issues
FROM issue AS i
JOIN issue_against_risk_erm AS ar ON ar.issue_id = i.issue_id
JOIN taxonomy_node_classifies_risk_erm AS c ON c.risk_id = ar.risk_id
JOIN taxonomy_node_parent_of_taxonomy_node_erm AS p3 ON p3.child_id = c.taxonomy_node_id
JOIN taxonomy_node_parent_of_taxonomy_node_erm AS p2 ON p2.child_id = p3.parent_id
JOIN taxonomy_node_erm AS l1 ON l1.taxonomy_node_id = p2.parent_id
WHERE i.source <> 'IA'
GROUP BY l1.taxonomy_node_id, l1.name, year
ORDER BY l1_node_id, year;

supporting.note: LEFT JOINs keep key controls that reach no unit; OPTIONAL MATCH does the same in Cypher.
supporting.question: Owner concentration: who owns the most key controls, and how many business units those controls reach (derived, not planted)
supporting.sql:
-- Supporting query: owner concentration of key controls
SELECT o.person_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.control_id) AS key_controls,
  COUNT(DISTINCT bo.business_unit_id) AS business_units
FROM owned_by AS o
JOIN control AS c ON c.control_id = o.control_id
LEFT JOIN mitigates AS mi ON mi.control_id = c.control_id
LEFT JOIN exposed_to AS ex ON ex.risk_id = mi.risk_id
LEFT JOIN business_unit_owns_auditable_entity AS bo
  ON bo.auditable_entity_id = ex.auditable_entity_id
WHERE c.key_control = 'Y'
GROUP BY o.person_id
ORDER BY key_controls DESC, business_units DESC, o.person_id
LIMIT 10;

counting: clauses: clause keywords as each language writes them; JOIN and Cypher writes are not clauses (a join counts once, as a step; a write once, as a moving part); OPTIONAL MATCH is a clause
steps: SQL FROM/JOIN targets minus one (every table named, including a CTE or a union branch's table); Cypher relationship patterns, *n and *m..n counting n hops

moving_parts follow one rule on both sides: extra SELECTs (CTE, subquery, union branch) or Cypher WITH stages, subqueries and UNION; recursion once per side (RECURSIVE, or an unbounded *); writes count once on both sides, as a moving part
disclosed exceptions: filtering after an aggregate (SQL HAVING is a clause; Cypher needs a WITH stage, one moving part more, in rounds 2 and 6); upserts (no round uses one)
a round with setup is scored as setup plus query
verdict_rule.margin_definition: max(score) - 1.25 * min(score); zero or more names a winner, negative is close
verdict_rule.verdict: SQL when SQL's score times 1.25 is at most Cypher's; graph the other way round; close otherwise

views.sql:
-- Shared views: one per relationship that ERM and IA publish as separate tables.
CREATE TEMP VIEW risk AS
SELECT 'ERM' AS source, risk_id, inherent_rating
FROM risk_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT 'IA', risk_id, inherent_rating
FROM risk_ia;
CREATE TEMP VIEW mitigates AS
SELECT control_id, risk_id
FROM control_mitigates_risk_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT control_id, risk_id
FROM control_mitigates_risk_ia;
CREATE TEMP VIEW exposed_to AS
SELECT auditable_entity_id, risk_id
FROM auditable_entity_exposed_to_risk_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT auditable_entity_id, risk_id
FROM auditable_entity_exposed_to_risk_ia;
CREATE TEMP VIEW against_risk AS
SELECT issue_id, risk_id
FROM issue_against_risk_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT issue_id, risk_id
FROM issue_against_risk_ia;
CREATE TEMP VIEW depends_on AS
SELECT control_id, system_id
FROM control_depends_on_system_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT control_id, system_id
FROM control_depends_on_system_ia;
CREATE TEMP VIEW requires AS
SELECT regulation_id, control_id
FROM regulation_requires_control_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT regulation_id, control_id
FROM regulation_requires_control_ia;
CREATE TEMP VIEW control AS
SELECT 'ERM' AS source, control_id, key_control
FROM control_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT 'IA', control_id, key_control
FROM control_ia;
CREATE TEMP VIEW owned_by AS
SELECT control_id, person_id
FROM control_owned_by_person_erm
UNION ALL
SELECT control_id, person_id
FROM control_owned_by_person_ia;
